answer: In an ocean of AI agents, a marketplace can weight governance votes by tokens locked for 30 days, rather than by identity count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight, so even at the zenith of a sybil campaign, extra names add no power. The common thread is scarce capital: an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens to gain influence, bearing the funding cost and price risk.
